lead: The useful pattern today is to let an agent propose and investigate, while keeping consequential decisions and proof of correctness outside the model. Arca describes long-running financial work that hands decisions and money movement to human advisers, and Google’s PageBreak validates vulnerability hypotheses with code-written exploit checks before reporting them. For your regulated-sector designs, compare these boundaries with your own approvals and deterministic controls; both examples are vendor or practitioner accounts, not independent efficacy studies.

items.title: Google’s PageBreak Project – Real-World Findings
items.summary: Google says its PageBreak agent pairs model-generated vulnerability hypotheses with specialised validators that execute real payloads against running applications; unverified findings are kept from product teams. Google reports more than 500 XSS vulnerabilities found across first-party web applications since the project entered full operation in January 2026, while noting its validators can miss vulnerability classes and complex cases.
items.so_what: Trial the propose-then-deterministically-validate pattern against your security testing workflow, keeping model hypotheses separate from reportable findings and measuring both false positives and missed cases.

items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.summary: Parameter Labs describes a chain in ChatGPT in which an HTML preview could send messages to a MathLive listener, inject unsanitised HTML and create an unsandboxed frame that ran JavaScript in the signed-in page. The researchers say the issue could expose private conversations and permit account actions; OpenAI fixed it on 26 October 2026 and classified the report as P1.
items.so_what: Review sandbox boundaries and message-origin validation anywhere untrusted previews share a page with privileged components, and require evidence that cross-frame messages cannot create trusted execution contexts.

items.title: Agents Prompt People: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work
items.summary: Arca’s lead AI engineer says agent tasks can span up to ten days, with persistent memory tracking work, hand-offs and responsible people. He describes an internally benchmarked model-selection harness, deterministic restrictions that reserve trading and money movement for human advisers, and a strict-format boundary between agent-written code and backend data; these are practitioner statements, not independent outcome measurements.
items.so_what: Benchmark the persistent-workflow and human-decision pattern against your current orchestration, and test whether any agent-generated data query is constrained by a typed, validated interface before it reaches sensitive systems.

items.title: Kubernetes Confidential Containers Get Fortanix Attestation and Key Management
items.summary: The article describes Fortanix connecting Kubernetes Confidential Containers workload attestation to conditional release of encryption keys for models and data in hardware-backed trusted execution environments. It says the integration is available now and can be deployed as a hosted service, on-premises or air-gapped; the article gives no price, and notes that attestation does not establish safe application behaviour or protect against denial of service and hardware side channels.
items.so_what: Benchmark the attestation-to-key-release pattern against Azure Secure Key Release and open-source Trustee for sensitive inference, documenting the guest software and application boundaries that hardware attestation does not cover.

items.title: Spring News Roundup: First Release Candidates of Boot, Framework, Data, Security, Modulith, AI
items.summary: InfoQ’s 31 October roundup covers first release candidates published during the week of 19 October, including Spring AI 2.1.0-RC1. The Spring AI candidate adds a SessionService interface in place of the deprecated ChatMemory interface and preserves ordered assistant-message parts for OpenAI and DeepSeek choices; these are release candidates, not general-availability releases, and the roundup states no pricing or hosting-region details.
items.so_what: Trial the session API and ordered-part behaviour in a non-production branch if Spring AI is in your stack, and test migration and provider-specific message handling before adopting the release candidate.

watch.title: datasette-llm 0.1a9
watch.note: The plugin now inherits LLM’s default model, reducing explicit setup for Datasette Agent; a small configuration convenience, so revisit only if evaluating that stack.
